meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and, but', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Есть много способов отлично начать день.
examples.trans: There are many ways to start the day great.
One can do sports.
Let us go play a game of chess instead.

examples.text: А можно просто насладиться минутой тишины.

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'enough', paired with 'хватать'.

examples.trans: Come on, enough!

meanings.note: Prefix 'из-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'виняться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'apologize'.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и извиняться вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and apologize on time.

examples.text: На нашей кухне все умеют извиняться.
examples.trans: In our kitchen everyone knows how to apologize.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what, that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Кажется, закончились у него бритвы. А что за обследование?
examples.trans: It seems he ran out of razors. And what kind of checkup is it?

examples.text: Что простите? Вы мне брюки будете стирать?
examples.trans: What do you mean forgive me? Are you going to wash my trousers?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'here', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ты его даже не читал! Он не будет здесь работать.
examples.trans: You did not even read it! He will not work here.
Spend the night here in comfort.

meanings.en: to happen, take place, go on
meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'исходить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'is happening', paired with 'произойти'.

examples.trans: What is going on here?
What is going on? I don't understand.

examples.text: Мы не знаем, что с нашей дочерью происходит!
examples.trans: We don't know what is happening with our daughter!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I will explain everything to them myself.

examples.text: Бабушка, всё ваше! Почему ты не рассказала про нас?
examples.trans: Grandma, it is all yours! Why did you not tell them about us?

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Everything is fine.
How are you? — OK.
Good! Everything's fine over there.

поругаться.gloss: to quarrel, to have a fight

meanings.en: to quarrel, to have an argument
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'ругаться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to quarrel, to have a fight', paired with 'ругаться'.

examples.trans: We will have a pretend quarrel in front of her.

examples.text: Нам нужно срочно поругаться перед ней.
examples.trans: We need to quarrel in front of her right away.

examples.text: Мы поругаемся понарошку, только для вида.
examples.trans: We will quarrel in pretend, only for show.
